metric: bits per byte at fixed compute

steps.action: Read instruction.md, environment/manifest.json and environment/nanogpt_substrate.json; record that the graded reading comes off a real 2200-step run of the canonical 12-layer 768-dimension decoder and that the denominator is the byte count of a slice you never see.
steps.establishes: what is graded and what is frozen

steps.action: Read environment/default_tokenizer.py and enumerate DEFAULT_OPTION_GRID; note that every row produces whole whitespace-delimited words only, and that the largest top_k it offers is 1024.
steps.establishes: the handed option set, and its structural limit

steps.action: Count the room. The vocabulary budget is the decoder's own vocab_size of 50304, of which 50048 entries are yours past the single bytes, so the handed grid leaves at least 49024 of them unspent at any option value.
steps.establishes: the option set is exhausted long before the budget is

steps.action: Note that the plateau cannot be swept out by brute force here: the verifier measures the handed construction itself, in the same pass, and no reading of it is published for you to aim just under.
steps.establishes: there is no literal to recall and no bar to reverse-engineer

steps.action: Re-read the objective. The step budget buys a fixed number of training tokens and the denominator is a byte count, so a vocabulary that expresses the same bytes in fewer tokens covers more corpus inside the budget and costs fewer predictions on the held-out slice.
steps.establishes: the derivation of the wider construction

steps.action: Measure what you can measure for free: encode a known slice of bytes under a candidate vocabulary and read its bytes-per-token, which needs no training at all.
steps.establishes: a cheap proxy for the quantity under your control

steps.action: Build the wider construction: greedy merges of the most frequent adjacent symbol pair over the decoded FineWeb bytes, ties broken lexicographically, stopping when no pair occurs twice or the budget is spent.
steps.establishes: affixes, whole words and multi-word phrases competing for the same budget on equal terms

steps.action: Declare no HALT_AT_STEPS, so the run reaches the bound step and the reading is asked to hold at the two verifier-scheduled points after it.
steps.establishes: the reading is sustained, not a transient dip

steps.action: Write submission/tokenizer.py exporting build_vocab and let the verifier train the decoder and compute the number.
steps.establishes: a graded reading the submission never touched
